title: What Is a Shaft Repair Sleeve?
meta_description: A shaft repair sleeve (wear sleeve) is a thin-walled sleeve that repairs a worn or damaged shaft seal surface so the original seal size works again. Here's how it works and when to use it.
body:
A shaft repair sleeve, also called a wear sleeve, is a thin-walled sleeve that installs over a worn or damaged shaft seal surface. When a shaft seal surface gets scored or worn, the seal can no longer hold. Instead of replacing the shaft, you press-on a sleeve that gives the seal a fresh counterface again.

## Why shafts wear

The shaft seal surface is one of the hardest-working, most exposed parts of a rotating machine. Over time, dirt, grit and the seal lip itself wear a groove into the shaft. Once that groove forms, the seal leaks, lubricant escapes and contamination gets in.

## Why a sleeve works

The whole point of a wear sleeve is that it restores the shaft to its original seal diameter without an expensive repair. Because it's thin-walled, you use the same seal size you already have. No machining. No shaft replacement. No engineering changes.

## What makes DuraSleeve different

DuraSleeve adds a hard chrome surface over an SAE/ANSI 304 stainless steel base. The hard chrome surface resists wear and reduces friction, and the stainless steel resists corrosion. DuraSleeve is made in North America from US Steel.

**The bottom line:** if you've got a worn shaft seal surface, a repair sleeve is the fast, low-cost fix. DuraSleeve is built to make that repair last.

title: How to Measure a Shaft for a Wear Sleeve
meta_description: Accurate measurement is the key to a good shaft sleeve fit. Measure the shaft in three places and use the average. Here's the right way to do it.
body:
Measuring a shaft the right way is the difference between a sleeve that fits and one that doesn't. Here's how to do it.

## Clean the shaft first

Wipe the shaft clean and remove any burrs or raised metal. A clean, smooth reading gives you a reliable measurement.

## Measure in three places

Take measurements around the shaft at the seal journal. Worn shafts aren't perfectly round — three readings give you the true average. Use a caliper or micrometer.

## Use the average

Add the three readings and divide by three. That average is the diameter you match to the sizing chart. The sleeve needs to press into the surface with an interference fit.

## Match the range

Every sleeve has a shaft diameter range. Pick the sleeve whose range covers your average measurement. If you're between sizes, check the chart carefully.

## Don't slide it on

A shaft repair sleeve is a press fit / interference fit. It should not slide on freely. If it does, re-check your measurement.

**The bottom line:** measure clean, take three readings, use the average, and match it to the sizing chart. That's how you get a reliable repair.

title: Why Shaft Seal Wear Happens (and How to Spot It)
meta_description: Shaft seal wear is caused by contamination, heat, misalignment and normal operation. Learn the signs and how a repair sleeve fixes the worn surface.
body:
Shaft seal wear is one of the most common maintenance problems in rotating equipment. It happens in predictable ways.

## The usual causes

Contamination is the biggest culprit. Dust, grit, sand and debris get behind the seal lip and grind a groove into the shaft. Heat degrades the seal and the surface. Misalignment and vibration put uneven load on the contact area.

## How the wear looks

A worn shaft seal surface usually shows a score line or groove right where the seal lip contacts. It may look polished, grooved, or pitted. Once it's there, the seal can't hold.

## Why it matters

A leaking seal lets lubricant out and contamination in. Left unchecked, that cascade leads to bearing failure, seal damage, and eventually catastrophic equipment failure. It usually starts at the seal contact area.

## The fix

Once the surface is worn, a repair sleeve is the fast fix. It restores the shaft to a fresh counterface using the same seal size. In real-world testing, DuraSleeve lasted at least 2x longer than a legacy sleeve.

**The bottom line:** seal surface wear is a groove in the most-exposed part of your shaft. Catch it early and a repair sleeve fixes it before it becomes a much bigger problem.
